articles.title: 15 亿美元要价太高，曝苹果 / 迪士尼放弃竞购 2030 及 2034 年男足世界杯美国转播权
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，CNBC 记者亚历克斯 · 谢尔曼（Alex Sherman）于 11 月 19 日爆料称，苹果和迪士尼将不参与 2030 年及 2034 年男足世界杯美国市场转播权竞标。报道指出价格是迪士尼止步的重要原因，这批版权预期价格超过 15 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 100.38 亿元人民币），而迪士尼还需为现有体育内容续约预留资金。迪士尼持有的美国职业橄榄球大联盟（NFL）、国家冰球联盟（NHL）和美国职业棒球大联盟（MLB）版权，都将在 2030 年前面临续约。IT之家援引博文介绍，苹果经常被视为热门体育版权的潜在买家，但实际出手一直较为谨慎。苹果与美国职业足球大联盟（MLS）的合作，是现有体育版权布局中金额最大的一项，合同最后三个完整赛季的费用据报为每年 2.5 亿美元（现汇率约合 16.73 亿元人民币）。此前，Skydance 也被曝放弃竞标，潜在买家阵容进一步收窄。Netflix、亚马逊、YouTube、福克斯和 NBC 环球仍是潜在竞标者，其中 NBC 环球尚未决定是否出价。

articles.title: 孙正义曾考虑万亿美元收购 SK 海力士？软银回应：已不再积极考虑
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，据《The Information》今日报道，软银集团董事长兼 CEO 孙正义近期曾接洽华尔街金融机构，探讨为收购韩国 SK 海力士筹集资金，潜在交易规模高达 1 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.69 万亿元人民币）。不过，软银发言人随后表示，该交易目前已不再处于积极考虑阶段。“软银会探索许多机会，而这笔交易目前已不再纳入积极考虑范围。”知情人士称，孙正义此前曾考虑通过收购 SK 海力士，进一步扩大软银在人工智能产业链中的布局。SK 海力士是全球主要存储芯片制造商之一，其生产的 HBM 是英伟达等厂商先进 AI 芯片的重要配套产品。报道指出，SK 海力士的全球市值目前约为 5,800 亿美元（现汇率约合 3.88 万亿元人民币），而其股价在一个月前曾处于更高水平。按照当时较高的市值计算，如果收购溢价达到通常交易中约 40% 的水平，整体交易估值将接近 1 万亿美元（现汇率约合 6.69 万亿元人民币）。不过，这笔交易面临明显的融资和监管障碍。《The Information》指出，软银此前已向 OpenAI 投入大量资金，资产负债表承压，目前尚不清楚孙正义将如何筹集如此庞大的收购资金，也没有迹象表明华尔街金融机构愿意为这笔交易提供融资。此外，SK 海力士由韩国 SK 集团控制，是韩国重要的科技资产。报道认为，韩国政府很可能不会允许总部位于日本的软银主导收购，尤其是考虑到韩国和美国均对本国关键技术资产的外国收购设有严格监管规定。况且，目前也没有迹象表明 SK 集团有意出售 SK 海力士。

articles.title: 腾讯混元姚顺雨团队：Hy4 仍有很大改进空间，计划训练更大规模模型
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，11 月 21 日凌晨，腾讯首席 AI 科学家、混元大模型负责人姚顺雨和团队成员，在 Reddit 进行了一场持续 120 分钟的 AMA，回答全球开发者关于混元的“任何问题”。问答环节，有人询问：字节跳动、Kimi 等似乎都在往 3 万亿、甚至 5 万亿参数的超大模型推进，而你们还在 7000 亿。为什么？你们怎么看参数量对模型能力的实际影响？这方面有什么计划？混元团队回应：“Hy3 和 Hy4 已经表明，做得扎实的小模型也能超过更大的模型。它们的成本也更低，而且在这个过程中，你能学到更多、收获更多。”不过，混元团队也表示，Hy4 仍有很大的改进空间，尤其是通过后训练。“我们正投入大量精力进行大规模强化学习，同时继续改善用户体验和模型安全。我们还计划训练更大规模的模型。”对于是否有可能推出 240 亿到 310 亿参数的稠密模型？该团队表示：“有可能，我们正在考虑。”对于是否会发布对标 Qwen 27B 稠密模型的小模型？发布 100B 以下、专门做编程的模型吗？该团队表示：“第一个，有可能。第二个，大概不会。”IT之家注：姚顺雨本科毕业于清华大学姚班，获普林斯顿大学计算机科学博士学位，2024 年加入 OpenAI 并参与智能体产品 operator 与 deep research 开发。其研究聚焦语言智能体与现实世界交互，提出 ReAct 方法首创“推理 — 行动”结合的智能体范式，被学术界与工业界广泛采纳。2025 年 12 月，腾讯升级大模型研发架构，新成立 AI Infra 部、AI Data 部、数据计算平台部，全面强化其大模型的研发体系与核心能力。姚顺雨出任“CEO / 总裁办公室”首席 AI 科学家，向腾讯总裁刘炽平汇报；同时兼任 AI Infra 部、大语言模型部负责人，向技术工程事业群总裁卢山汇报。今年 7 月，腾讯宣布混元多模态模型部门与大语言模型部门合并，成立基础模型部，统一由姚顺雨管理，以进一步提升模型研发和协同效率，探索全模态模型的智能上限。

articles.title: Win11 学院：如何在 Windows 11 26x00.10075 开启 WinUI 原生重构版搜索体验
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 今天（11 月 21 日）发布博文，报道称在 11 月可选更新 KB5132057 中，微软邀请部分 Windows 11 用户体验原生重构的 Windows Search 搜索体验。Windows 11 26H2 中基于 WinUI 的全新搜索功能。底层架构方面，新版 Windows Search 搜索摆脱旧版对 WebView2 网页组件的依赖，采用 WinUI 3 原生 UI 框架打造。WinUI 3 属于 Windows App SDK，使用基于 XAML 的界面模型，支持 C++ 和 C# 开发。该框架提供原生控件、布局、输入处理以及现代 Windows 风格的视觉效果。新版 Windows 11 搜索不包含任何 WebView2 元素。尽管任务栏位于右侧，Windows 11 搜索窗口仍会显示在底部中央。在资源占用方面，由于原先由网页运行环境承担的界面工作，现在交给原生 UI 框架处理，从而减少与网页容器相关的资源和初始化开销。IT之家附上相关视频如下：微软官方表示具体取决于使用场景，新版搜索的内存占用约降低 15%~20%。而根据该媒体实测，新版 Windows Search 打开速度更快，而且相比较旧版，还减轻了输入时的轻微迟滞。Windows 11 新搜索的启动动画。界面上，微软 Windows 11 新版搜索取消了常驻的大面积右侧预览区，改用紧凑的单列结果，搜索框位于底部，窗口大小随结果数量调整。在旧版搜索框中搜索文件会浪费大量空间。旧版搜索应用会遵循任务栏位置。在功能方面，新版搜索还具备“动手”能力，用户不仅能查找应用和文件，还能直接在搜索结果中调节亮度、切换深色模式、开启蓝牙或静音，减少进入设置页面的步骤。推送方面，微软目前尚未向所有 Windows 11 用户开放该功能，不过安装 KB5132057 可选更新后，Windows 11 用户可以借助 ViveTool 工具启用。1.确保 Windows 11 系统版本号不低于 26200.10075 或 26300.10075 版本。2. 从 GitHub 页面下载 ViveTool 工具，然后解压缩到任意文件夹，但需要记住该文件夹路径（例如 C:\Program Files (x86)\ViVeTool-v0.3.4）。3. 按下 Win 键（或者使用鼠标）打开开始菜单，输入“cmd”，然后选择“以管理员权限”打开命令提示符。4. 使用 cd 命令跳转到 ViveTool 文件夹，例如“cd C:\Program Files (x86)\ViVeTool-v0.3.4”5. 然后输入相关命令，按下回车键。vivetool /enable /id:61161304继续输入以下命令，第一个 ID 用于启用 11 月更新的功能包，第二个 ID 用于启用新的 Windows 搜索：vivetool /enable /id:583813416. 重启设备。相关阅读：《解锁微软 Win11 开发版隐藏新功能，开源命令行工具 ViveTool 使用指南》《微软推送 Win11 26x00.10075 可选更新：重构搜索体验，内存占用降低 15%~20%》

articles.title: 美国 SpaceX 龙飞船脱离空间站启程返回地球，携大量科研样本和设备
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，美国太空探索技术公司（SpaceX）货运“龙”飞船 20 日脱离国际空间站，携大量科研样本和设备等启程返回地球。据美国航空航天局介绍，“龙”飞船于美国东部时间 20 日 12 时 05 分许（北京时间 21 日 1 时 05 分许）脱离国际空间站，预计于美国西部时间 21 日 13 时 55 分许（北京时间 22 日 5 时 55 分许）在加利福尼亚州附近海域溅落。其重返大气层和溅落时将不会有直播。IT之家查询获悉，该飞船于 10 月 13 日发射，10 月 15 日抵达国际空间站，为航天员送去超过 6300 磅（2860 公斤）的食品、科研设备与补给。返回时，飞船将带回数千磅货物。NASA 在 11 月 17 日的更新中表示，其中包括用于研究太空与地面血管衰老、心血管疾病的 3D 生物打印血管结构等科研样本。本次任务是 SpaceX 为 NASA 商业补给服务计划执行的第 35 次飞行。

articles.title: 全球仅此一件：马斯克到访上海工厂收到员工特制“边角料手办”，陶琳晒图
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，特斯拉公司副总裁陶琳昨晚在微博发文称，CEO 埃隆 · 马斯克当天到访特斯拉上海超级工厂期间，收到一份由工厂员工自行设计、手工制作的“限量手办”，全球仅此一件。据介绍，这款作品使用特斯拉生产过程中的边角材料制成，将特斯拉车型与上海城市特色元素组合在一起。陶琳介绍称，这件手办最初只是工厂员工利用业余时间推进的创意项目，随后被作为纪念品赠送给马斯克，马斯克对其设计表示喜欢。IT之家注：所谓“边角料”，指车身冲压、内饰裁切等工序中产生的余料，并非可独立流通的原材料。此次上海之行是马斯克 24 小时中国行的一部分。他此前在深圳参加 2026 年 APEC 相关活动，随后专程飞往上海。马斯克在工厂对员工表示：“我想来上海，感谢亚太以及中国团队。”这是他自 2023 年以来首次到访特斯拉上海超级工厂。据陶琳披露，马斯克与员工交流了辅助驾驶技术进展和人形机器人业务，称“辅助驾驶技术进展一日千里，人形机器人正在快速提升各项技能”。他对上海超级工厂的制造实力和中国团队的执行力、制造水准表示赞赏。上海工厂目前仍处于满产状态。乘联分会数据显示，特斯拉中国 10 月批发销量为 67829 辆，同比增长 10.3%，连续第 12 个月实现同比正增长。马斯克此次到访距他上一次视察上海工厂已过去约三年，而特斯拉第三代人形机器人 Optimus 刚在一个月前进入初期爬坡阶段，他在 11 月 9 日还曾透露特斯拉可能以出租而非出售的方式提供 Optimus 机器人。相关阅读：《特斯拉副总裁陶琳：马斯克 24 小时中国行专门从深圳飞到上海，对上海超级工厂赞赏有加》

articles.title: 拯救爆满的“下载”文件夹：微软 Win11 将推 AI 整理神器，授权后可查找 / 分类 / 移动 / 重命名文件
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 昨日（11 月 20 日）发布博文，报道称在 Ignite 2026 活动中，微软展示 Copilot“本地文件操作”功能，在征得用户授权后可以查找、分类、移动或重命名本地文件。IT之家附上相关视频如下：微软表示该功能可以减少手动翻找和归类的麻烦，用户主动启用并授权后，即可用日常语言要求 AI 查找、移动文件、创建文件和文件夹，还能根据文件内容批量重命名。在本次演示中，微软为了便于和团队成员分享内容，要求将“下载”文件夹里的分析师报告整理到 OneDrive。微软 Copilot 请求权限后，扫描相关目录，在 OneDrive 中创建“Analyst Reports”文件夹，随后逐一移入 8 份 PDF，并列出移动记录，提供撤销按钮。报道指出，演示中的 8 份文件，其名称均未直接出现“分析师报告”字样，Copilot 通过读取内容识别出符合要求的资料。用户因此不必记住准确文件名，只需描述要找什么，再由 AI 完成筛选与整理。在权限边界方面，演示中的授权界面提供“暂不允许”和“仅本次会话允许”两个选项，没有“始终允许”，且访问范围限于当前对话及相关目录，无法一次授权便能读取整台电脑。

articles.title: 英伟达发布 GeForce 621.35 热修复驱动，修复 SSD 后台异常写入问题
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，英伟达于当地时间 11 月 20 日发布了 GeForce Hotfix 621.35 显卡驱动，修复此前部分 Game Ready 驱动可能在后台向固态硬盘（SSD）过度写入数据的问题。这一热修复驱动基于最新的 GeForce Game Ready Driver 621.24 版本，仅包含一项修复：解决后台可能向 nvlog.nvlgstg 文件过度写入数据的问题，对应 Bug 编号为 7116722。此前，有用户反馈，安装 GeForce 621.14 和 621.24 驱动后，即使电脑处于空闲状态，系统仍会持续产生大量 SSD 写入操作。相关问题涉及 NVDisplayContainer.exe 进程，该进程会反复改写 nvlog.nvlgstg 日志文件。据 TechPowerUp 报道，部分用户测得的异常写入量最高达到每小时 30GB，而此前的 621.01 版本驱动在相同的 5 分钟空闲时间内，日志写入量约为 2MB。此次发布的 621.35 属于可选热修驱动，采用缩短后的质量测试流程，并非正式 WHQL 认证版本。英伟达表示，热修驱动主要用于提前向用户提供针对性问题修复，相关修复内容后续还会整合进正式驱动。此次 621.35 热修驱动面向 Windows 10 和 Windows 11 64 位系统提供下载，用户需要通过英伟达官方客户支持页面获取，目前不通过 NVIDIA App 分发。IT之家附下载地址：https://international.download.nvidia.com/Windows/621.35hf/621.35-desktop-notebook-win10-win11-64bit-international-dch.hf.exe相关阅读：《英伟达发布 Game Ready 621.14 驱动：优化〈魔兽世界：无限〉，修复视频黑屏问题》《英伟达承认 GeForce 621.01 驱动存在问题：播放视频时可能卡住或黑屏》《最高每小时狂写 30GB：英伟达 621.24 驱动反馈加速消耗 SSD 寿命》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，荣耀 700/700 Pro 手机将于 11 月 23 日 14:30 发布，博主 @数码闲聊站 今日对新机的核心配置进行了曝光汇总。IT之家整理如下：6.57"1.5K+120Hz LTPS 直屏，0.98mm 四等边，1.59" 原生背屏骁龙 8s Gen4 / 骁龙 8 Gen5 处理器9000mAh 电池 +80W 有线充，Pro 支持 50W 无线充200Mp 1/1.56" 主摄 +12Mp 超广角 +50Mp 3.5X 潜望长焦，200mm 迷你增距镜IP68/IP69/IP69K，光学指纹，机身厚 7.96mm / 重 211gIT之家注意到，荣耀官网显示，荣耀 700 系列手机此次有“三杯”，分别是荣耀 700 Pro、荣耀 700、荣耀 700S，全系采用背屏设计。该机将搭载 9000mAh 青海湖电池，背屏支持后置自拍、AI 互动、多样主题，以及心率、血氧检测以及航班提醒等功能。此外，荣耀 700 系列手机将支持荣耀长焦增距镜 G200，号称同档位首款。据介绍，荣耀 700 系列搭配增距镜使用时，可使用 15 倍舞台 Live 模式拍摄，号称“看台也能出神图”。

articles.title: 安卓手机有望变身 Win11 PC 副屏，微软“连接至 Windows”新功能曝光
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 昨日（11 月 20 日）发布博文，报道称微软正酝酿升级安卓版“连接至 Windows”（Link to Windows）应用，开发“扩展显示”（Extend display）功能，有望让安卓手机变身电脑副屏。该媒体指出和当前将手机投屏到电脑显示器上相反，“扩展显示”将部分电脑桌面传送到手机上，为用户额外增加一块显示区域。例如手机可用于放置聊天窗口；如果平板获得支持，更大的屏幕则适合显示参考文档，让闲置设备有机会重新派上用场。该媒体通过挖掘最新安卓版“连接至 Windows”应用程序，在界面文字、图标及代码中发现相关线索。其中相关代码包含 H.264、HEVC 视频编码格式，以及分辨率、刷新率等参数字段，意味着该功能可能通过视频传输呈现电脑画面。IT之家附上相关代码如下：应用中还出现了停止显示、连续按两次返回键退出等操作提示，代码也列出了电脑锁定、连接中断等结束会话的情况。不过，部分接收与连接代码仍不完整，功能尚处于开发阶段。相比之下，苹果 Sidecar（随航）支持将 iPad 用作 Mac 副屏，但不支持 iPhone。微软这项功能若能落地，将为安卓手机与 Windows 电脑协作增加新用途。

articles.title: 蔚来 ES9 地平线鎏金特别版上市：24K 鎏金车标，售 63.8 万元起
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，在蔚来品牌及品牌标识发布十周年之际，蔚来 ES9 地平线鎏金特别版正式上市，售价 63.8 万元起；采用 BaaS 电池租用方式购买，售价 53 万元起。据官方介绍，该车提供鎏金拂晓、鎏金晨曦、鎏金朗照配色，搭载鎏金双叠地平线腰线。历经 8 次喷涂、5 次烘烤，多重色漆与清漆层层叠加，再经 12 道工序、109 小时精细打磨。此外，该车还提供 24K 鎏金银色车标、24K 鎏金玄金车标，搭配 24K 鎏金悬浮轮标及 22 英寸锻造揽月轮圈。座舱方面，该车带来全新双色内饰主题「苏木红」搭配「云贝米」，以及「可可棕」搭配「帕米尔棕」，行业首次引入「金属绣线」辅以插针绣工艺。据IT之家此前报道，蔚来 ES9 旗舰 SUV 于 5 月 27 日上市，整车购买价格为 49.8 万-62.8 万起，租电方案价格为 39 万-52 万元起：行政豪华版：整车购买 49.8 万元起、电池租用方式购买 39 万元起行政签名版：整车购买 55.8 万元起、电池租用方式购买 45 万元起地平线特别版：整车购买 62.8 万元起、电池租用方式购买 52 万元起该车长 5365mm，宽 2029mm，高 1870mm，轴距达到 3250mm，号称中国体量最大的纯电 SUV。蔚来 ES9 搭载了最新一代全域 900V 高压架构，峰值功率 520kW、峰值扭矩 700N·m；搭载自研高性能六活塞制动卡钳，100-0km/h 制动距离 35.3m；标配 102kWh 长续航电池，CLTC 综合工况续航里程 620km；搭载线控转向系统、全主动悬架的天行智能底盘，并标配后轮转向（转弯半径 5.4 米）。

articles.title: 微软发布 Win11 26340.10032 等预览版：新增 People 小组件、优化蓝牙 LE Audio 立体声输出
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，微软昨天（11 月 20 日）发布博文，邀请 Beta、Experimental 频道的 Windows Insider 项目成员，测试适用于 Windows 11 的多个预览版更新。本次推送的版本分别为：Beta 通道（26H2）：最新预览版 Build 26320.10022Beta 通道（26H1）：最新预览版 Build 28020.3562Experimental 通道（26H2）：最新预览版 Build 26340.10032Experimental 通道（26H1）：最新预览版 Build 28120.3571Experimental 通道（未来平台）：最新预览版 Build 29712.1013上周暂停频道迁移后，Insider 现已可从 Beta、Experimental 频道切换至 Experimental（未来平台）频道，需注意 Experimental（未来平台）版本不匹配任何零售版 Win11，切换或退出该频道需完全重装系统。IT之家附 Windows 11 改进进展如下：1、蓝牙 LE Audio 音频优化（Experimental 频道）蓝牙 LE Audio 设备在启用麦克风时，可实现全范围立体声保真输出，保证游戏语音、语音通话、语音输入、Copilot Chat 语音聊天场景下的高质量音频体验。当使用支持超宽带立体声（Super Wideband Stereo）的 LE Audio 设备搭配兼容 PC 时，可在设置 > 系统 > 声音 > 输出 > 对应蓝牙设备 > 输出设置 > 麦克风启用时格式中，选择 2 声道、16 位、48000Hz 选项。该功能适用于支持 48kHz 播放的 LE Audio 耳机、耳塞、音箱设备。若遇到兼容性问题，可通过反馈中心提交反馈。2、新增 People 小组件（Experimental 频道）新增 People 小组件，可从小部件面板快速访问常用联系人，整合支持的通讯应用中的相关联系人，方便快速继续对话。使用时可通过 Windows 键 + W 打开小部件面板，点击 + 号打开小部件选择器，添加 People 小组件后，点击对应联系人即可跳转至支持的通讯应用打开会话。前置要求：需先在 PC 上安装配置手机连接（Phone Link）、WhatsApp 或二者同时配置，才能在小组件中显示联系人。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，小米新推出的米家扫振电动牙刷 2（Pro 版此前已开售）已于昨日正式开售，建议零售价 199 元，首发 175 元，叠加国补后 149 元，下单享 2 年质保、评价晒单返 10 元京豆。京东米家声波扫振电动牙刷 2 白色 148.75 元直达链接这款产品搭载升级声波扫振马达 2.0，驱动刷头做大摆角扫振运动，模拟巴氏刷牙法的清洁轨迹，振动频率约 24000 次 / 分钟，可边扫边振清除牙菌斑，相比上代产品马达性能有所提升。其机身内置三轴高精度传感器，支持 4 区漏刷识别功能，配合机身 LED 分区灯环实时追踪刷牙轨迹：白灯提示已清洁区域，橙灯提示漏刷及未刷净区域，同时搭载 30 秒换区提醒，可及时引导用户补刷清洁盲区。米家扫振电动牙刷 2 配备全效缓震双刷头：清洁刷头采用月牙型剪裁，搭配优质菱形刷丝可深入齿缝深度净齿；刷头采用外高内低的刷丝排布，刷丝尖端直径细至 0.02mm 并添加含氟成分，温和贴合牙龈线。刷头底部包裹食品接触级软胶，软度相比普通材质提升 25%，支持 45° 弯曲，无铜植毛结构防锈更健康，刷丝自带褪色提醒功能，提示用户每 3 个月更换刷头。机身采用轻量化小巧设计，整机长度 236mm，相比上代产品缩短约 15mm；提供白色、粉色、绿色、蓝色 4 种配色可选，适配不同用户的审美偏好。续航方面，产品内置大容量电池，使用呵护模式满电可支持约 180 天日常使用、清洁模式约 100 天续航（按每日使用 2 次、每次 2 分钟测试），配备通用 Type-C 充电口，约 6 小时即可充满；整机达到 IPX8 级防水，密封结构支持刷完直接冲洗。该产品提供 3 种刷牙模式可选：呵护模式温和护龈，适配牙龈敏感人群与新手；清洁模式满足日常基础洁净需求；亮白模式深度清洁牙齿表面色素沉着。同时支持模式记忆功能，每次开机自动沿用上次设置的力度；开机 3 秒渐强启动，避免牙膏飞溅；充电口带潮湿检测功能，可及时提醒充电安全。IT之家附详细参数如下：京东米家扫振电动牙刷 2 Pro 彩屏数显提醒 190 天续航 智能分面扫振 情侣生日礼物 紫色 198.98 元直达链接

articles.title: 英伟达董事会为何对黄仁勋态度转变？婚外情无关紧要，核心问题在于诚信
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，据《连线》（WIRED）今日报道，英伟达董事会最终决定接受黄仁勋的辞职，主要原因并不在于婚外情，而是董事会认为他在相关事件中多次存在撒谎行为，导致董事会对其诚信和信任产生严重质疑。两名知情人士向《连线》透露，黄仁勋于 11 月 8 日承认存在婚外情，但当时董事会仍无法确定相关事件涉及的其他问题。同一天，英伟达董事会宣布启动独立调查。然而，接下来几天，随着更多婚外情指控浮出水面，其中包括一段据称涉及黄仁勋直接下属的关系，董事会的态度发生了变化。一名接近董事会的知情人士表示，能够确定的是，黄仁勋存在撒谎行为，而且这一情况持续约一年，从 2025 年 10 月一直延续到近期事件曝光。据知情人士透露，早在《纽约时报》2025 年 10 月首次报道英伟达与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 存在异常紧密的业务关系后，董事会成员就曾向黄仁勋询问他与一名女商人之间的关系。当时，黄仁勋向董事会否认双方存在任何不正当关系。随着婚外情事件曝光，英伟达董事会成员对此感到愤怒。一名了解董事会想法的人士告诉《连线》，最终促使董事会采取行动的主要原因是黄仁勋的撒谎行为。“这是一个关系到诚信和信任的问题。”此前，《连线》及其他媒体已经披露了英伟达董事会决定接受黄仁勋辞职的多项因素，但董事会将其缺乏坦诚视为主要原因，此前并未得到如此明确的披露。英伟达董事会主席哈维 · 琼斯（Harvey Jones）没有回应媒体的置评请求，英伟达发言人约翰 · 里佐（John Rizzo）拒绝置评。代表黄仁勋的公关公司 Trident 副总裁约翰 · 费舍尔（John Fisher）同样拒绝置评，仅表示黄仁勋是自愿辞去在英伟达的职务。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，比亚迪今日公布闪充网络最新运营数据：截至 11 月 20 日，全国累计上线闪充枪 31014 个，覆盖 345 座城市，闪充总用户数超过 357 万人。截至 9 月 30 日，比亚迪闪充网络累计上线 9009 座闪充站、21214 把枪，覆盖 342 座城市，用户数约 183 万。不到两个月，枪数增加近万把，用户规模接近翻倍。截至 10 月 7 日，闪充站数量为 12165 座，其中高速站 2111 座。比亚迪闪充技术于 2026 年 3 月 5 日发布，配套单枪峰值功率 1500kW 的闪充桩，配合第二代刀片电池，常温下电量从 10% 充至 97% 用时 9 分钟，零下 30℃ 环境下从 20% 充至 97% 约需 12 分钟。IT之家注：闪充枪即闪充桩上的单根充电终端，比亚迪闪充桩采用双枪设计，一把面向闪充车型，另一把兼容国标社会车辆。按照比亚迪“闪充中国”战略，该公司将在 2026 年底前建成 20000 座闪充站，由 18000 座城区“站中站”和 2000 座高速站构成。城区站目标覆盖 90% 区域，确保 5 公里内可找到闪充服务。闪充桩兼容全品牌国标车型，支持即插即充和无感支付。

articles.title: 近 200 万条请求揭开 AI 隐私漏洞：“零数据保留”也会泄密
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，科技媒体 Ars Technica 今天（11 月 21 日）发布博文，报道称安全公司 Dragos 首席研究官 HD Moore 向多家 AI 服务商发送近 200 万条带有可追踪“诱饵”的请求，发现 AI 服务链存在黑客窃取提示词、转售商泄露数据及未遵守隐私设置等问题。研究人员故意把一批可追踪的“测试秘密”（并非从真实用户渠道收集）发给 AI，观察之后有没有其他程序或人拿它们去访问系统，从而判断数据是否流出、可能从哪条服务链流出。调查发现，至少三家服务商出现遭入侵迹象，攻击者利用窃取的诱饵密钥发起数万次云服务接口调用，尝试寻找更多凭证、开通服务并维持访问权限。部分密钥在提交后数小时内便被使用，甚至有请求在模型运行前已遭拒绝，其中的密钥仍被盗走。风险还来自层层转手的服务链。许多 AI 应用通过中间商分配请求，内容可能经过多个平台，并在各环节解密处理。研究还发现，部分转售商记录并外传请求；一些标记“零数据保留”或“禁止数据收集”的请求，其私密网址仍在数日后遭到抓取。Moore 建议，敏感业务可考虑本地部署；无法自建的用户应尽量直接选择可信服务商，并明确指定上游提供方。IT之家附上参考地址Three breaches, endless leaks: Your AI supply chain needs canaries

articles.title: OpenAI 公布反蒸馏防护进展：GPT-6.2 Astra 思考链提取成功率从 54% 降至 0.2%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，当地时间 11 月 20 日，OpenAI 发布公告介绍了针对「对抗性蒸馏」（Adversarial Distillation）的防御措施。OpenAI 称其已加强 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 对内部推理思考链（Chain-of-Thought）的保护，以降低其他模型通过提取推理过程获取其能力的风险。OpenAI 表示，对抗性蒸馏是指未经授权地利用前沿 AI 模型的输出训练其他模型，使后者获得相似能力，却不具备原模型相应的安全防护。该行为可能导致网络安全、生物学等领域的高风险能力被转移到安全限制较弱的模型中。在内部自适应黑盒红队测试中，OpenAI 测试了攻击者提取模型此前请求和当前请求中受保护推理内容的成功率。结果显示，针对此前请求推理内容的提取成功率，从 GPT-6 Astra 原有安全机制下的 54.0%，降至 GPT-6.2 Astra 更新安全机制后的 0.2%；针对当前请求推理内容的提取成功率，则从 22.9% 降至 0.9%。测试结果汇总了 6 个攻击模型的数据。为实现上述防护，OpenAI 采用了多层措施，包括通过对抗性训练让模型识别并拒绝推理链提取请求，利用输入和输出分类器检测相关攻击及推理内容泄露，以及通过 API 限制不同会话、模型和组织之间的推理内容复用。IT之家附图如下：其中，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 会将受保护的推理内容与生成它的对话历史关联起来。如果此前的消息被修改，API 会丢弃基于该消息生成的后续推理内容。此外，安全防护较弱的旧版模型也无法读取这两个新模型的受保护推理内容。在针对相关行为的执法方面，OpenAI 称，今年以来，公司每周都会对涉及未经授权蒸馏活动的账号采取措施，规模从数千个到数万个不等，今年夏季以来相关执法规模明显增加。公司还会调查协调进行大规模提取的账号网络，并与其他模型提供商分享攻击指标，以协助识别相关滥用行为。OpenAI 还介绍了其对蒸馏安全风险的研究。公司内部测试发现，与仅使用模型最终回答、推理摘要和工具交互记录训练的学生模型相比，使用教师模型完整推理轨迹进行监督微调的学生模型，通常能够获得更好的网络安全能力迁移效果。相关阅读：《菲尔兹奖得主邓煜评论 AI 公司反蒸馏：你不能只在你蒸馏全人类知识时支持蒸馏》《英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋回应 AI 模型蒸馏争议：这是市场竞争行为》《商务部回应美方所谓 AI 蒸馏指控：于事无凭于法无据，典型双重标准》《消息称张一鸣内部下死命令：就算模型暂时落后，字节跳动也不会依赖 AI 蒸馏技术》《微软 CEO 纳德拉批评 AI 模型公司“双标”：一边主张“合理使用”数据，一边限制他人蒸馏》

articles.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. articles.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. articles.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. articles.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23398v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever.
  To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse compute architectures. articles.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, complex S-parameters at 201 frequency points, a structural category, and an RF response label. Building on these aligned representations, we define seven tasks spanning specification-conditioned layout generation, representation translation, response prediction, simulator-based validation, design diagnosis and improvement, structural understanding, and response classification. articles.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23445v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage pointwise projections and depthwise layers. Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generalized, human-in-the-loop framework for generating rigorous, curriculum-constrained mathematics assessment drafts. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer layer during prefill, BOS Summary relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query row alone, letting BOS aggregate all visual and textual input tokens into a self-derived context representation while every other token retains standard causal attention. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answers and requiring no additional task executions. Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. arXiv:2611.23564v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When LLM agents pass intermediate judgments downstream without uncertainty, later decisions may treat tentative assumptions as facts. Effective uncertainty propagation must preserve information for correction and update inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives. Yet scalar scores omit information needed for revision, while detailed descriptions and reflection incur additional costs. We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions. Building on this, we propose LProp (Latent Uncertainty Propagation), which revises inherited answer distributions using latent representations and new evidence without additional trajectory sampling. We evaluate both methods across multiple-choice, yes/no, open-ended question answering, and mathematical reasoning tasks. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $\tau^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $\tau^2$-bench. Abstract: Generator-based sparse adversarial attacks train encoder--decoder networks to produce transferable sparse perturbations for black-box robustness evaluation. Abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. articles.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
  The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study active exploration for minimax transition estimation in unknown Markov decision processes (MDPs). Frequentist $\kappa$-Explorer~\citep{gu2026kappa} addresses this problem through a parameterized family of exploration objectives, but requires confidence-bound constructions and joint optimization over plausible transition kernels and occupancy measures, introducing a computational burden that limits its practical applicability. We develop Bayesian $\kappa$-Explorer, which simplifies this procedure by placing Dirichlet priors on the transition distributions. Under the posterior mean estimator, the posterior expected squared $\ell_2$ error equals the total posterior variance, providing a closed-form exploration signal. articles.title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. However, a single sparse representation in traditional SAEs is responsible for both reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, which are not guaranteed to align. To separate these objectives, we propose DualSAE, a modular framework that augments standard SAEs with a plug-in Residual Branch. A standard SAE serves as the Sparse Branch, learning a sparse code that contains the dominant semantics of the input. The added Residual Branch models the non-semantic information omitted by the Sparse Branch. We ensure that the contributions of the two branches towards the overall reconstruction have minimal overlap through a decorrelation loss. Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) optimization depends on global properties of the underlying PDE and how the physics residual evolves across the domain. Standard optimizers such as Adam use fixed gradient-based statistics, while learned PINN optimizers replace the fixed rule with a learned update built from local parameters and optimization-history features. However, none explicitly use PDE-level information. We study two coupled design questions: what PDE-level information should a learned optimizer observe, and how should that information influence its update? We introduce an 11-dimensional PDE state-capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, and use it to condition a structured meta-learned optimizer through bounded feature-wise modulation. articles.title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $\varphi$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $\varphi$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.

Abstract: Long event streams require identifying each change and applying the changes in order. We train a selector on a frozen language model to read each transition. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25235v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24943v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this end, we introduce LLM Complexity, a new metric designed to quantify problem complexity from the perspective of LLMs by characterizing the area bounded above by the accuracy-token curve. Abstract: The rise of powerful, fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) necessitates robust natural language inference (NLI) systems. These NLI systems ideally train across various tasks, encompassing diverse concepts like sentiment analysis, news classification, and coreference resolution. However, this continual, multi-tasking approach can lead to catastrophic forgetting, where previously learned tasks are lost, especially in domains lacking specific labels. Rehearsing past examples with labels can further exacerbate this issue by causing overfitting, hindering the system's ability to classify new categories. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24960v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Converting complex documents into structured knowledge constitutes the critical infrastructure urgently required for deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in downstream research. However, blind to the Table of Contents (ToC) as a macro-structure, existing bottom-up paradigms rely on localized visual cues, inducing heuristic fragility in high-entropy layouts where visual prominence decouples from logical depth; meanwhile, direct LLM extraction lacks spatial grounding, triggering hallucinations in long contexts. We also introduce GLA5 and GDN2, which improve gated linear attention and Gated DeltaNet with low-rank output gates. articles.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. Under moderate to aggressive compression ratios, including up to 90%, PRKV achieves competitive task performance against established eviction baselines while reducing peak memory usage with low end-to-end overhead. These results demonstrate that multi-hop global influence estimation yields a favorable accuracy--memory trade-off for scalable long-context inference.

Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. However, these gains are not free: in practical deployments, longer prompts directly increase inference cost and latency. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. While prior work has often focused on how many examples to include in ICL, we study the complementary question of whether the available budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or on a larger number of shorter ones. We study this aspect in question answering (QA), by organizing candidate demonstrations into length-based bins and constructing prompts from examples within the same length range under fixed budgets. Abstract: We present No-Harm-Jury, a jury-based automated evaluation framework that scores AI-generated medical responses across seven conceptually distinct harm dimensions using a panel of five diverse language models as independent jurors. Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. While local CUAs feature robust baseline proficiency in single-step action prediction, they frequently fail at critical junctions due to rigid action loops or premature DONE decisions. Rather than imposing imprecise cognitive loads through textual reflection, CANDID repurposes parallel test-time scaling into a disciplined, execution-level intervention at sparse, failure-prone points. We introduce a loop-recovery mechanism to filter candidates away from repeated behaviors and a conservative, unanimous DONE gating policy that requires absolute consensus to terminate. Abstract: Populations vary along cultural dimensions such as individualism, collectivism, and honor. Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. articles.content:

Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). An LLM converted into a decision model answers a typed question about a response ("is the final answer correct?", "which step is the first error?") with a probability distribution, read in one forward pass, debiased over option orders and calibrated with about a hundred labels. Abstract: Understanding an egocentric environment requires reasoning about how surrounding entities affect the observer's actions. EgoPass-Bench comprises 284 manually reviewed evaluation clips recorded using Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) smart glasses and 2,201 distinct questions across five tasks assessing motion perception, interaction judgments about specified entities, and relevant-entity discovery without target cues. articles.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25061v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference. While fast, this pattern-matching approach degrades when faced with out-of-distribution (OOD) scene conditions unseen during training. Inspired by the generative nature of human vision, we propose Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input. To prevent degenerate flat outputs, we couple the generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting network that constrains the optimization space to a valid, multi-view-consistent 3D manifold. Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. A fixed paired-teacher filter retains samples answered correctly from an evidence-centered positive crop but incorrectly from a spatially displaced negative crop. At the token level, both EMA teachers score the same student-generated response, and their absolute log-probability differences measure view sensitivity. articles.content:

Abstract: Localizing object boundaries is important for embodied visual systems, since small boundary errors can change the inferred geometry of physical surfaces. We study whether deep stereo models produce boundaries consistent with simple shape priors when local image and disparity cues are weak. We create a synthetic stereo dataset consisting of objects drawn from a highly constrained family of shapes, with randomized depth, slant, color and texture. Despite the simplicity of this shape space, we find that several state-of-the-art stereo models retain systematic boundary errors, even when finetuned or trained from scratch on the dataset. We then introduce a simple generative stereo model that jointly predicts disparity and a distance field representing object boundaries. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cross-modal knowledge distillation can incur negative transfer when source-modality supervision conflicts with the target modality's discriminative characteristics. We propose TALD, a two-stage framework for Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement in class-aligned logit space. Guided by task-dependent self-benefiting and cross-modal exclusivity criteria, a Residual Disentangler decomposes logits from a teacher and an independently trained target-modality reference student into modality-general and modality-specific components. A Sample-Adaptive Modulator regulates decomposition constraints and sample-specific fusion weights. The learned modality-general components are then adaptively fused to supervise the final student. Across five benchmarks spanning vision, audio, and text, TALD achieves the largest mean accuracy gain and highest positive-transfer frequency among the compared methods. articles.title: What a Calibrated Probability Hides: Belief-Level Post-Training for Decision Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A calibrated decision model can predict how often each answer is chosen. The same prediction can reflect disagreement among people who are confident in their choices or uncertainty among people who share a belief. Disagreement calls for identifying whose perspective applies, while uncertainty calls for gathering more evidence. Standard post-training scores a single prediction against one observed choice at a time, learning the pooled distribution without distinguishing these two sources of uncertainty. We introduce Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization (BGPO). The policy proposes a list of beliefs, estimates their prevalence, and predicts a choice distribution for each. During training, BGPO uses Bayes' rule to estimate how likely each belief was to generate an observed choice. These estimates weight the choice's contribution to each belief's log-score reward. Abstract: JEPA-based video encoders learn strong representations for video and image understanding through prediction in latent space. However, their standard pretraining predicts features within individual images or video clips, without explicitly exploiting paired camera views of the same object or moment. Consequently, the learned representations may not reliably support matching across different camera viewpoints. To solve this problem, we introduce multi-view predictive post-training to strengthen cross-view instance and temporal correspondence while retaining independent single-view inference. A shared encoder processes masked context views independently, and a training-time predictor jointly predicts latent tokens for masked context regions and a fully held-out view. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. articles.title: Identity World Model: Recognizing People in an Imagined Latent World
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole-body human recognition has advanced rapidly with large vision models. However, existing methods remain fragile under real-world variations, as they tie identity to transient cues such as clothing, texture, pose, or viewpoint. We argue that a robust recognizer should not merely learn to ignore these cues, but imagine how a person would be represented if they changed. To this end, we propose IDWorld, an identity world model: just as a latent world model predicts the features of a scene after an action, IDWorld predicts how a person would be represented under a changed condition. In a single forward pass, IDWorld imagines these counterfactual features under shared canonical conditions, such as the same outfit, a fixed view, or a bare silhouette, without rendering any pixels. articles.title: Recurrent Vision Language Models Solve the Shell Game
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tracking a hidden object through a video is effortless for humans, yet it remains a bottleneck for vision language models (VLMs). In the shell game, where a ball is hidden under one of several identical cups that are then swapped, VLMs that answer directly stay near chance, thinking models fail on long games, and fine-tuning learns only the lengths it has seen. We argue that the limit is serial computation: each swap must be composed with the last result, and a VLM of fixed depth has only a fixed number of state transitions for it. To address this, we propose RecurrentVLM, which makes every attention layer of a pretrained VLM recur over time by computing the keys and values of finished frame groups from the layer's own output. With a single answer token, RecurrentVLM reaches 100% on VET-Bench and 99.6% on MET-Bench, and 99% on 50-swap games after training on at most 30 swaps. Abstract: Reliable visual perception under degradation requires distinguishing task-relevant content from degradation-induced variations, especially in concealed object segmentation (COS), where foreground cues are inherently weak. The central challenge is not merely improving visibility, but identifying reliable content evidence amid degradation-induced variations. RGB-space segmentation often entangles content and degradation cues, while restoration-based methods primarily focus on image recovery and task interaction. This motivates explicit factorization to distinguish content evidence from degradation effects and assess its reliability. Abstract: Can a distilled image generator save time by reusing features between its few remaining denoising steps? One full trajectory and one raw-cache trajectory from the same initial noise supply a scalar correction for each branch type and reuse position. Abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. Abstract: We propose the radiometric camera, a model that lifts any central geometric camera model to a radiometric one. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion Transformers generate high-quality images, but iterative sampling remains computationally expensive. Feature caching reduces the number of full network evaluations, yet its approximation error can become more severe under short sampling schedules, where fewer full-compute steps and a coarser sampling grid can make history-based extrapolation less reliable. In this paper, we propose CalibCache, a lightweight offline calibration method that corrects systematic discrepancies between cached and full-compute feature dynamics. Specifically, CalibCache calibrates feature acceleration, defined as the second-order finite difference across sampling steps. Using only a single pair of full-compute and naive-cache trajectories at each setting, CalibCache fits scalar acceleration maps offline by centered least squares. Abstract: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past. We test whether this is justified: we implement sixteen textbook planners, each combining a path source (reference line, A*, hybrid A*, RRT*) with a trajectory method (Frenet lattice, nonlinear optimization, $s$--$t$ search, dynamic window), and evaluate them on three benchmarks: open loop on nuScenes, closed loop on nuPlan with ground-truth perception, and photorealistic closed loop on HUGSIM. On HUGSIM, they replace only the planner of the end-to-end model UniAD and read its frozen perception, without an HD map or other privileged information. articles.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL. To add constraints to an already trained policy, we keep a PPO teacher's backbone and replace its action head with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses. We then distill the student with DAgger in the teacher's self-play simulator. Over 9 seeds, the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes. For a stronger teacher, the student has fewer failures on nuPlan and Waymo, while staying level on CARLA. Its distillation takes no more than 30% of the teacher's training time.

Abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25215v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. Abstract: Ferrofluids are liquids containing magnetic nanoparticles, enabling shape control through external magnetic fields. This deformability supports their use as soft robotic bodies that can navigate confined spaces and manipulate objects. Their nonlinear continuum dynamics, however, make reliable control challenging. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25243v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures. This work presents a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making. A simplified quadrotor follows scripted trajectories while co-located virtual sensors generate synchronized RGB, RTX LiDAR, and illustrative IR-like observations. The testbed varies target range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability, with future stress cases including sensor dropout, temporal misalignment, cross-modal disagreement, and false observations. Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25202v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. It unpacks this territory with a 3i-framework, the Interface, where operators and swarms work together, the Infrastructure, where organisations distribute tasks, decisions and blame, and the Imaginary, where law, policy and shared societal assumptions define what a crisis is and which interventions it justifies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25320v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. articles.content:
arXiv:2509.21961v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Learning-based planners are sensitive to the long-tailed distribution of driving data. Common maneuvers dominate datasets, while dangerous or rare scenarios are sparse. This imbalance can bias models toward the frequent cases and degrade performance on critical scenarios. To tackle this problem, we compare balancing strategies for sampling training data and find reweighting by trajectory pattern an effective approach. We then present FlowDrive, a flow-matching trajectory planner that learns a conditional rectified flow to map noise directly to trajectory distributions with few flow-matching steps. We further introduce moderated, in-the-loop guidance that injects small perturbation between flow steps to systematically increase trajectory diversity while remaining scene-consistent. articles.content:
arXiv:2602.07629v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose LCLA (Language-Conditioned Latent Alignment), a framework for vision-language navigation that learns modular perception-action interfaces by aligning sensory observations to a latent representation of an expert policy. The expert is first trained with privileged state information, inducing a latent space sufficient for control, after which its latent interface and action head are frozen. A lightweight adapter is then trained to map raw visual-language observations, via a frozen vision-language model, into the expert's latent space, reducing the problem of visuomotor learning to supervised latent alignment rather than end-to-end policy optimization. This decoupling enforces a stable contract between perception and control, enabling expert behavior to be reused across sensing modalities and environmental variations. articles.content:
arXiv:2602.18224v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often bundle architectural changes with different pretraining data, backbone scales, and optimization recipes, obscuring what actually drives progress. We introduce SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA, a standard vision-language backbone with a lightweight continuous-action head, as a controlled testbed for this attribution problem; our contribution is methodological and empirical (a controlled attribution study and a minimal-baseline calibration), not a new technique. articles.title: 商汤20%资源投入背后的逻辑：林达华谈拼手速与长期竞争力
articles.content: Scaling Law在空间智能这里失效了？    作者丨周蕾    编辑丨岑峰                                                                                                       今年初字节的Seedance 2.0发布时，“电影级别”的出片质量让不少从业者倍感兴奋和震撼，新的创作蓝图正在他们面前徐徐展开——但对商汤的Seko团队来说，那是一段“迷茫”的日子。商汤联合创始人、首席科学家林达华在最近一次访谈中回忆，那段时间他去见投资人、参加行业会议，被问到的几乎总是同一个问题：你们的Seko和Seedance有什么区别？做得过它吗？团队里一度出现自我怀疑的声音：这件事还要不要做下去？后来故事并没有走向商汤Seko单枪匹马“对抗”Seedance的结局。Seedance把30秒的视频片段渲染到顶级水准；而Seko面向的创作者，最终交付的是100集的短剧——这中间隔着剧本、分镜、人物设定和跨剧集的形象一致性，是一整套创作流程。想清楚了这件事，Seko反而活得更好了：据林达华在访谈中透露，今年这款产品的用户增长了7到8倍，平台上产出了播放量过亿的短剧。对于商汤在大模型市场上的声量，林达华自己有个坦率的评价：“可能不是最大的”。这家公司的路线，也始终没有完全跟着行业最热的方向走。但商汤有一个坚持多年的习惯：直到今天，公司依然有20%的资源，投入给没有任何产品出口的预研工作。某种程度来说，这也是一种“播种”，种子下地时其实无需承诺收成。汤晓鸥常挂在嘴边的那句话——life finds a way，“生命自寻出路”，或许正是这笔投入的逻辑。在最近参加的微博科技 X 卫诗婕联合出品的《科技漫谈》栏目访谈中，林达华从行业的现状聊起，穿过商业化的验证，最后落在智能的边界上。但贯穿始终的线索只有一个：那20%的资源，以及支撑它的判断——为什么有的路值得走得很长、很久，哪怕眼下仍未看见出口。01训练成本停不下来，拼手速的中国AI大模型行业的钱，正在以一种停不下来的方式烧下去。行业里曾经有一个普遍假设：花巨大代价训出一个好模型，成本就能摊薄到之后的规模化服务里。林达华在访谈中指出，这个假设未必成立——问题不在模型不够好，而是“你不继续训下一个，别人就会超过你”。竞争逼着公司一轮接一轮地重训，训练成本因此停不下来，而且越滚越大。尽管过去一年的行业叙事，几乎被“更大即更强”占据，但卷参数这条路正在遭到反噬。他提到两个信号：一是模型的体量选择变得更务实。最近各家厂商均发布了Flash级别的中小模型：GLM 5.3 Flash、DeepSeek 4.1 Flash，谷歌和OpenAI也推出了同类规格的产品。林达华在访谈中特别提到了DeepSeek的表现：“4.1的Flash，它的性能水平是比4.0 Pro是要好的。”一个几百B量级、训练调优精良的模型跑赢上一代Pro，说明中等体量上的优化空间还远没有吃完。二是预训练数据的质量被重新摆上桌面。当几千亿参数的模型在实战中跑赢了2万亿参数的对手，很多人开始回头检查自己的数据管线。林达华对此有一个形象的解释：“（数据里）有很多的杂质、很多的东西相互打架，使得中间的很多的效率就会被抵扣掉。”结果就是一个又贵又不理想的模型，参数堆上去了，效果没上去。“当所有人很盲目地去做参数量的竞争，我觉得并不是一种健康的状态。”在他看来，这两个信号意味着行业正在回归理性：不再围着单一指标较劲，而是回到最终用户的价值上。上一轮AI周期里，类似情况也出现过，商汤自己就是亲历者。每个项目都要从收集数据开始，专门训练、调优、测试，全流程重做一遍，很难真正复制。只是当年的计量单位是项目，今天换成了参数。拼手速是另一种内卷的形态。美国的前沿实验室定义着SOTA的天花板，新模型一发布，等于给中国的从业者们指了一条路——国内往往在两三个月内涌出一批宣称采用同类方案的产品，抢占生态位，最近大热的RSI（递归自我改进）同样是一堆公司在同时开建。“说实话，拼手速这个事其实是蛮累的。”林达华观察

articles.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
articles.content: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

articles.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

articles.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
articles.content: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

articles.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
articles.content: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

articles.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
articles.content: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.

articles.title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement
articles.content: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.

articles.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
articles.content: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

articles.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
articles.content: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most challenging activity classes. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity generation in a pretrained encoder's representation space is achievable and practically useful for cross-subject HAR augmentation.

articles.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
articles.content: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

articles.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
articles.content: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.
